dataset.description:
We aim to estimate the impacts of air pollution on mortality and hospital admissions in urban areas. To this end, we will associate daily mean concentrations of particulate matter (PM), and components such as ultrafine particles (aerodynamic diameter < 100nm) and black carbon (BC), with daily counts of mortality and hospital admissions from 27 cities. The cities included in the study are: Barcelona, Granada, Madrid (Spain); Athens (Greece); London and Birmingham (United Kingdom); Augsburg, Dresden, Langen and Leipzig (Germany); Paris, Grenoble, Marseille and Lille (France); Zurich, Bern and Lugano (Switzerland); Budapest (Hungary); Helsinki (Finland); Beijing (China); Rochester (USA); Prague (Czech Republic); Stockholm (Sweden); Bucharest (Romania); Coimbra (Portugal); Moscow and Saint Petersburg (Russia).


We will have two datasets for each of the above-mentioned cities, one of daily mortality counts, and one of hospital admission counts. The datasets will be named mort_[city_name].txt and hosp_[city_name].txt, respectively, and will contain information on the gender of the patient, date of admission or death, cause of admission or death, and age (grouped as 0-74, +75 years). The study will consider deaths by natural causes, and cardiovascular and respiratory diseases – classified by the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD-10) as A00-R99, I00-I99 and J00-J99, respectively. The hospital admission dataset will also focus on cardiovascular and respiratory diseases as causes of hospitalization.


The mortality and hospital admission datasets will be requested from the corresponding health authorities in each city through confidentiality agreements that prevent data sharing. The health data will be stored in a password-secured server in ISGlobal and cannot be shared with third parties without previous consent from the corresponding health authorities.

dataset.description: EBAS is a database hosting observation data of atmospheric chemical composition and physical properties. EBAS hosts data submitted by data originators in support of a number of national and international programs ranging from monitoring activities to research projects. EBAS is developed and operated by the Norwegian Institute for Air Research (NILU).
